takeaway: A robot arm is a chain: each motor moves everything after it, so the motors nearest the base work hardest.

selfCheck.question: Which motor would you make the strongest, and why?
selfCheck.answer: I would make the shoulder lift the strongest. It holds up everything after it: the elbow, both wrist motors, the gripper and whatever the gripper carries. When the arm reaches out, all that weight is far from the shoulder, so the shoulder has to work hardest just to keep the arm still. Step 3 shows this with numbers: the shoulder lift uses 31%, compared with 24% for the elbow and 6% for the wrist bend.

sentence: A robot arm is a row of rigid plastic parts joined by motors, one motor at each joint. Each motor has to hold up every part beyond it, and the motor nearest the base holds up the most. That is why the strongest motors go near the base, and why the tip of the arm can only lift light things.
